market_context: The session has become an uneven rebound: SPY has recovered from $726.79 to $733.00, QQQ is up 0.65% and IWM is up 1.04%, while DIA and NVDA lag and VIX falls 7.15%. Nvidia cleared its earnings bar but its shares reversed, leaving Anthropic's IPO pricing and the 2 p.m. Fed minutes as the principal late-session catalysts, with the 10-year Treasury yield still elevated at 5.06% (finance.yahoo.com).

predictions.reasoning: SPY's recovery from $727.91 at 11:22 a.m. to $733.00, alongside a lower VIX and stronger QQQ and IWM, points to improving intraday risk appetite. Intraday bond buying also accompanied easing yields, supporting a small further gain, although the Fed minutes could quickly reverse the move ([tradevae.com).

The Nasdaq was up approximately 0.5% early in the afternoon after two consecutive declines, and current megacap breadth is favorable: AMZN is up 3.63%, TSLA 1.59%, GOOGL 1.23%, MSFT 0.58%, and AAPL 0.51%. That broad support should outweigh NVDA's drag into the close, though Fed-minutes volatility limits conviction (finance.yahoo.com).

AMZN is the strongest listed megacap, up 3.63% and trading near its $267.97 session high after being up only about 2% in Benzinga's earlier sector update. Consumer discretionary and growth are leading, and AMZN's continued intraday advancement favors a modest extension rather than a late reversal (benzinga.com).

NVDA has faded from $159.70 to $152.06, close to its $150.85 session low, even after revenue surged 103% year over year; Yahoo reports it was on pace to extend a four-day losing streak. That bearish response to strong earnings, together with earlier declines of roughly 1% in SMH and SOXX, favors additional mild weakness into the close (finance.yahoo.com).
